findings.description: AC-3's template declares app/req/res and stub handlers but no free value variables; response.md block 1 uses `id`/`created` and block 2 uses `user`/`user1`/`user2`. These are wave 3 calls, so AC-4 gives no skip reason for them and they will fail to compile unless the template also declares stub values (e.g. `Object user, user1, user2, created; String id;`) or the docs declare them. Does not block AC-7: response.md blocks 4-5 (`res.status(204).end()`, `res.status(302).header(...).end()`) and routing.md block 4 (Method.of/MethodSet, already in NaruServe-api) compile with the current template.

implementability.evidence: Gradle runs on JDK 17 with no toolchain override, so ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler() is non-null and `--release 8` matches configureCompile (build.gradle:35); AC-1 needs one testImplementation line next to junit/gradleTestKit (build.gradle:240-243). Harness is new code but small.

evidence_strength.evidence: Method.of / Method.get / MethodSet already exist in NaruServe-api main; response.md blocks 4-5 and routing.md blocks 1,4,5 use only wave 3 methods (res.status/header/end, app.route/get, MethodSet).

dependency_health.evidence: OPS-HTTP-001 and IR-HTTP-001 are planned and only about to move to evolving; Request/Response/RestApp/RouteHandler/RouteBuilder signatures are not yet in code.

ac_verifiability.evidence: In-process compile with fixed imports, staleness check (AC-6) and the AC-7 floor (>=1 compiled block per file) are mechanically testable; gap is undeclared free variables (V2-001).

scope_fit.evidence: One root test plus one build line and fence relabels; skip list bounds later-wave content across ~69 java blocks.

product_fit.evidence: Keeps docs/api examples honest per CLAUDE.md docs rule; JVM-side only, no runtime impact.
